question: A 68-year-old male visits his primary care physician after an episode of syncope during a tennis match. He reports exertional dyspnea with mild substernal chest pain. On physical exam a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur is heard best at the right 2nd intercostal space. This murmur was not heard at the patient's last appointment six months ago. Which of the following would most support a diagnosis of aortic stenosis?

options.opb: Murmur radiates to carotid arteries bilaterally
options.ope: Double pulsation of the carotid pulse

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur at right 2nd intercostal space" -> "Possible aortic stenosis" -> "Increased risk of syncope due to reduced cardiac output" -> "Increased risk of exertional dyspnea and chest pain" -> "Likely aortic stenosis" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The presence of a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the right 2nd intercostal space in a 68-year-old male, along with symptoms of exertional dyspnea and chest pain, strongly supports a diagnosis of aortic stenosis. The murmur not being present six months ago further raises suspicion. The option 'Murmur radiates to carotid arteries bilaterally' would most support the diagnosis of aortic stenosis as this characteristic radiation pattern is typical for aortic stenosis.
analysis: The core medical principle here is the clinical presentation of aortic stenosis, characterized by a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the right 2nd intercostal space, along with exertional dyspnea and chest pain. The option 'Murmur radiates to carotid arteries bilaterally' aligns with the typical radiation pattern seen in aortic stenosis, supporting the diagnosis.
